NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the Mayor has called a Special Meeting of the City Council pursuant to
Government Code section 54956, to be called to order concurrent with the regular City Council meeting in the
Council Chambers at City Hall at 6:00 p.m. on Tuesday, July 11, 2023. The agenda for the Special Meeting adds
to the regular agenda New Business item 8C and Closed Session item 13A as set forth below.

Posted by the office of the City Clerk on Monday, July 10, 2023 at 4:00 p.m.

*CLOSED SESSION WILL COMMENCE AT 6:00PM AND REGULAR AGENDA WILL
COMMENCE AT 7:00PM

NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under City Council Meeting agendas at rhe.city and during regular
  business hours in the office of the City Clerk. Meetings are live broadcast on the City's website and a
  recording is available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP-TV Channel 35
  (Cox) and Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome in-person on any item during City Council consideration of the item. Public
  correspondence may also be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestates.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record. Members of the public may also comment online using
  eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos” page of the City’s website
  (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment” button next
  to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After you
  register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
  public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the record.

  An opportunity is also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If
  you would like to address the City Council regarding an item on this agenda or make a general public
  comment, please complete a speaker sheet and give to the City Clerk.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JULY 11, 2023

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR HUFF called the meeting to order at 7:05 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Silver Spur Little League.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  Brown Schachter

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Public Works Director David Wahba
  Community Development Director Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson
  Administrative Aide Gabrielle Swain

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

MAYOR HUFF provided comments regarding the recent land movement on Peartree Lane,
explaining that on Saturday, July 8, there was significant land movement resulting in twelve
homes being red-tagged and evacuated, displacing 16 residents She reported that late this
afternoon, due to a break in a sewer main line, five additional housing units have been ordered
to evacuate. MAYOR HUFF stated that the City has officially activated its Emergency
Operations Center (EOC), noting that this remains an active situation, and all residents are
being provided with assistance to find shelter if needed.

**ITEM TAKEN OUT OF ORDER**

No public testimony was received.

A.  ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 2557 APPROVING A CITY SPORTS FIELD USE
  AND ALLOCATION POLICY

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2557 approving a City
  Sports Field Use and Allocation Policy.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA thanked the Subcommittee members for their input on this
policy.

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ echoed COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA’s sentiments,
emphasizing the months of thoughtfulness put into this policy in order for it to be as equitable
as possible to all groups who share the fields.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
Public testimony was received from Michael Diehl, Silver Spur Little League President-Elect,
expressing concern that the League’s contract and the proposed policy conflict.

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ stated that the policy is a general policy for use of the fields by
all sports and parties and outlined the timeline in developing this policy.

Public testimony was also received from Peter Cho, Silver Spur Little League Vice-President,
echoing Mr. Diehl’s concerns.

Assistant City Manager Davis explained that the City works with four different youth sports
organizations, noting the policy is meant to address the use of the fields by all groups, and that
the policy will work together with the League’s agreement. City Attorney Davis added that the
City reviewed the agreement with the League, and that the policy is a supplement to that
agreement.

Further public testimony was received by resident Dave Gerard. MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ
explained all of the considerations that were put into the creation of the policy and noted that
non-profits such as the League cannot be compared to Club sports which are run for-profit.

Lastly, public testimony was received by two unidentified residents expressing concerns about
the policy.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN thanked the Subcommittee for their work on this policy and
encouraged the League to work with staff who are collaborative and will help work through any
concerns they may have.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA stated that there was an identified need for a policy, and that
the policy is incredibly well thought out and is a living document.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2557 APPROVING A CITY SPORTS FIELD USE
  AND ALLOCATION POLICY.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Brown Schachter

City Clerk Pettit read Resolution No. 2557 by title.
